newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends steady, U.S. gasoline supports.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends steady, U.S. gasoline supports.

text.p: IPE Brent crude ended steady on Monday, supported by firmer U.S. markets and modest short-covering after Friday's heavy sell-off, brokers said.
Mar Brent closed at $22.54 a barrel, up two cents and 19 cents off the low of $22.35. The contract lost 66 cents Friday.
"(NYMEX) gasoline gave some support, WTI (crude) gave support but we were also expecting a bit of a bounce after Friday's collapse," said a broker.
Brokers said IPE dealing was subdued in the absence of fresh fundamental news which they said was needed to prompt a break-out at either end of the $22-$23.00 a barrel range.
"It's been very slow, one of those non-days," said one.
U.S. traders said healthy demand for gasoline on Gulf coast spot markets helped lift the NYMEX March contract by 0.14 cents to close at 68.40 cents a gallon.
Forecasts of a return to colder weather for the United States also helped provide support to heating oil, which had threatened to lead the market lower again, brokers said.
"Talk of some cold weather again helped heat(ing oil) just when it was beginning to look pretty nasty," said one.
The eastern United States could be hit by an Arctic blast next week, meteorologists said on Monday.

"It is going to whack the eastern half (of the U.S.), from the eastern Plains to the eastern Seaboard next Tuesday and Wednesday. Temperatures will be much below normal," said Fred Gesser, chief forecaster for Weather Express Inc.

Earlier, IPE Feb gas oil closed $5.25 weaker at $204.00 a tonne, just 50 cents off the session low as slack demand on northwest European spot markets and early weakness on U.S. heating oil futures took their toll.
